title: Close a named gas cylinder's valve and lock it with a cylinder lockout cap
instruction: Close the valve of the argon cylinder, the one with the dark green shoulder: turn its handwheel clockwise, seen from above, until it stops. Then lower the red cylinder lockout cap over that valve, swing the cap's locking plate shut around the valve's neck, put the blue padlock's shackle through the two tabs and snap it shut. Do not touch the oxygen cylinder, the one with the white shoulder.
context: Before a gas line or regulator is worked on, the cylinder feeding it is closed at its valve and locked out: a cap over the valve, padlocked round its neck, stops anyone reopening it. Closing or locking the wrong cylinder, or leaving the cap on without a padlock, lets the gas be turned back on onto the work.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Cylinders: two empty industrial gas cylinders (steel, 18.4 cm across) stand in wells so that only their tops show: each shoulder rises through a 20.8 cm round opening in the table to 2.5 cm above it, topped by a steel neck ring (the cap-thread collar, 8.0 cm across) from 2.0 to 5.5 cm. The wells keep the valves within the arms' reach; a rebuild can use cut-off cylinder tops (shoulder, neck ring and valve) fixed to the table. The argon cylinder's valve axis is 30 cm in front of the bases and 4 cm right of the midline; the oxygen cylinder's is 30 cm in front and 21 cm left. Shoulders are painted as in EN 1089-3: argon dark green (RAL 6001), oxygen white (RAL 9010), each with a shoulder label (6 x 2.6 cm, ARGON white on green, OXYGEN black on white) on the side facing the robot, tilted 35 degrees back. Valves: Sherwood GSV-class brass handwheel cylinder valves: the inlet stem (27 mm across) shows 14 mm above the neck ring (5.5 to 6.9 cm), then a 42 mm square wrench block (6.9 to 8.3 cm), a 30 mm square body up to 10.6 cm with the CGA outlet pointing left (its face 36 mm from the axis, centred 9.3 cm up), the bonnet and a 57 mm six-lobed aluminium handwheel from 11.4 to 12.8 cm with a dark mark on one lobe. Both valves are open half a turn (180 degrees anticlockwise from seated, seen from above); turning a handwheel takes 1.1 N m. Lockout: a red Brady LM023E gas cylinder lockout (polypropylene can, 88 mm across, 159 mm tall, closed at the top, 0.2 kg) stands open end down on a grey stand, its axis 25 cm in front of the bases and 9 cm left of the midline, its rim 6.0 cm above the table. Its 4 mm locking plate lies under the open end on a rivet at the rim on the side away from the robot and starts swung 150 degrees open, out to the back right. Shut, the 33 mm round end of the plate's keyhole is on the can's axis and a tab on the plate (24 mm tall, standing 20 mm out from the can's side, 9.5 mm hole) lies against a matching tab on the can, both on the side facing the robot. The stand is a grey steel horseshoe that holds the rim on the side away from the plate, on a column. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (blue, 410BLU; body 38 x 45 x 19 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle with 38 mm vertical and 19 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg), open (shackle popped up 16 mm, key in the cylinder), lies on its 38 x 44 mm face on a grey pedestal (a 1.2 x 1.6 cm column on a 5 x 5 x 1 cm foot) whose 3.8 x 2.2 cm top slopes 15 degrees down toward the right, about 10 cm above the table; body centre 13 cm in front of the bases and 25 cm left of the midline, shackle pointing right, short leg on the far side. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, the oxygen valve's handwheel turns 15 degrees or more, the argon valve is turned back open 30 degrees or more after being closed (before the padlock is shut), or the cap is fitted over the oxygen valve with its plate shut. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the argon handwheel is seated (within 5 degrees of its stop); 0.5 if, with it seated, the cap is over the argon valve (its axis within 1 cm of the valve's, tilted less than 10 degrees, its rim 3.5 to 14.5 mm above the neck ring, so the plate is level with the gap under the wrench block); 0.75 if the plate is also shut (within 8 degrees) round the valve's neck; 1.0 if the padlock's shackle is also snapped shut through both tabs' holes and the after-release check passes. Dropping the padlock or the cap is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock and 7.4 cm from the cap's axis for 1 s: holding the can, push the plate's tab toward open with a spring scale at 10 N (about 0.94 N m about the rivet) and keep pushing; after 1.5 s also twist the cap anticlockwise with 1 N m through a quarter turn (it turns freely on the valve); then also pull the cap straight up with 20 N for 1.5 s (stop once it has risen 2 cm). Pass if the plate stays within 15 degrees of shut, the cap rises less than 15 mm, the argon handwheel stays within 5 degrees of seated and the padlock still hangs shut from the can's tab; if not, the score is 0.75. Angles are read from a photo taken from above with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and take it off the tabs; swing the cap's plate open (about 150 degrees, out to the back right), lift the cap off and stand it back on its stand with the plate still open; close the padlock's shackle to its popped-up position and lay it back on its pedestal, shackle toward the right. Open the argon valve half a turn (anticlockwise from above, the dark mark on its handwheel pointing the same way as at the start) and check the oxygen valve is still open half a turn. No gas is used: the cylinders are empty (or inert-gas cylinders capped downstream). About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, station arm gains. Lock chain is geometry: the plate's 33 mm keyhole under the 42 mm wrench block stops the lift, the can covers the handwheel, a shackle through both tabs stops the plate. Handwheel 1.1 N m (Sherwood's low end; no 2.2-3.3 N m seating peak), open half a turn. Box colliders, stepped keyhole; padlock latch by rule; cylinders in wells; check forces applied after recording. Details in README.
